steps.title: Open the dashboard
steps.narration: Every page opens with one simple answer: is today's board safe to rely on? A quiet green strip right under the header gives the verdict before you look at anything else.
steps.point_out: The green "GO — today's board is current." strip just below the header.

steps.title: Browse the stock leaderboard
steps.narration: The leaderboard ranks hundreds of companies, and every score carries an honest evidence status instead of a bare number.
steps.point_out: 541 of 541 candidates scored, each showing a plain "Not yet proven" badge next to its signal.

steps.title: Drill into one stock's evidence
steps.narration: Opening a single name like NVDA carries the same honesty right down to the individual stock page — nothing gets dressed up once you zoom in.
steps.point_out: The "Not yet proven" evidence status sitting right next to NVDA's scores.

steps.title: See up to thirty years of price history
steps.narration: One click on the chart's full-range control reveals nearly three decades of price history for this stock, honestly bounded to what actually exists for the name.
steps.point_out: The chart redraws to 3,025 daily bars — close to thirty years of history.

steps.title: Audit the evidence ledger
steps.narration: The Evidence page is the single source of truth for every trading idea ever tested, including the honest record of the ones that didn't hold up.
steps.point_out: The leadership_score entry, plainly marked FAIL with its real -0.03% out-of-sample result and test date.

steps.title: Check how much of the market is covered
steps.narration: The Data Manager page shows exactly how wide and how current the underlying dataset is, in plain numbers.
steps.point_out: 590 symbols tracked, with the full coverage panel laid out underneath.

steps.title: Open the research hub
steps.narration: The Research hub is where the deeper bookkeeping lives — how much testing budget remains, and every idea ever put on record.
steps.point_out: A "Certification-budget accounting" card sitting alongside the research labs.

steps.title: See the statistics budget before it's spent
steps.narration: One click into the budget panel shows exactly how much statistical rigor has been used so far, and how much is left before the next idea can be tested.
steps.point_out: The trial counter reading "Next canonical trial will be #8," next to the required-significance and remaining-budget figures.

steps.title: Your watchlist carries the same guarantee
steps.narration: A personal shortlist gets covered by the exact same daily check as every other page — nothing is exempt.
steps.point_out: The identical GO strip sitting above the watchlist table.

steps.title: Evidence that knows the market's mood
steps.narration: Back on the Evidence page, a different kind of check shows up: some ideas are only ever tested inside one kind of market, and the ledger keeps track of exactly which one.
steps.point_out: A "Regime: Risk-on" tag on the Breakout-watch entry, still honestly marked FAIL.

steps.title: Combined signals get tested too
steps.narration: It's not just single signals under the microscope — pairing two ideas together is held to the exact same bar.
steps.point_out: The "rs_spy_3m × high_proximity — composite" entry, tested together and still marked FAIL.

steps.title: A broad, point-in-time universe
steps.narration: Back on the Data Manager page, the candidate list isn't a fixed set frozen in time — it's tracked as it actually changed across the full thirty-year history.
steps.point_out: The dynamic-universe membership timeline underneath the coverage numbers.

steps.title: Decades of market context, each one sourced
steps.narration: Index and macro context go just as deep as the stock data, and every series is labeled with exactly where it came from.
steps.point_out: The "Index & benchmark data provenance" panel, naming each vendor down to the FRED-sourced macro proxy.

steps.title: Every registered idea, discoverable in one place
steps.narration: Before any idea can be tested, it has to be written down first — and that registry is one click away from the research hub.
steps.point_out: A "Pre-registration registry" link sitting on the Research hub page.

steps.title: Open the pre-registration registry
steps.narration: Opening the registry shows every hypothesis exactly as it was written down before testing began — nothing gets added after the fact.
steps.point_out: The registered vcp_contraction hypothesis, with its selectors and registration date.

steps.title: Browse the rejected-ideas graveyard
steps.narration: Every idea that didn't survive testing stays on record too, so nobody wastes time re-testing something already ruled out.
steps.point_out: The negative-results graveyard listing every rejected hypothesis.

steps.title: Jump from a rejected idea straight to its record
steps.narration: Clicking a rejected idea in the graveyard jumps straight to its exact entry in the registry — the two records stay linked, not just filed separately.
steps.point_out: The registry scrolling to and highlighting the matching leadership_score entry.
